commands.notes: Must be started before running any ROS nodes

Record all topics

commands.title: ros2 run
commands.desc: Run a node from the specified package

options.desc: Load parameters from a YAML file
Set a parameter directly on the command line (-p is short for --param)
Set the log level (debug / info / warn / error / fatal)
Remap topic/service names

commands.title: ros2 launch
commands.desc: Launch multiple nodes from a launch file

commands.title: ros2 doctor
commands.desc: Check whether the ROS 2 environment is configured correctly, and report potential issues with environment variables, network, system settings, etc.

options.desc: Generate a full diagnostic report
Exit with a non-zero status when an error is found

commands.title: ros2 pkg list
commands.desc: List all available packages in the current environment
commands.notes: Filter with grep, e.g. ros2 pkg list | grep turtlesim

commands.title: ros2 pkg prefix
commands.desc: Return the installation directory of a package, useful for locating its source code or resources

commands.title: ros2 pkg executables
commands.desc: List all executables provided by a package
commands.notes: Without a package name, lists executables of all packages; with a package name, only that package's

commands.title: ros2 pkg create
commands.desc: Create a new ROS 2 package
commands.example:
# Create a Python package with dependencies and a node file
ros2 pkg create my_package --build-type ament_python --dependencies std_msgs --node-name my_node
# Create a package with license, description, and maintainer info
ros2 pkg create my_robot_pkg --license Apache-2.0 --description "My robot description" --maintainer-email "you@example.com" --maintainer-name "Your Name"

options.desc: Specify the build type (ament_python / ament_cmake / ament_cmake_python)
Specify dependency packages, e.g. --dependencies rclpy std_msgs
Also create a node file
Specify the license, e.g. Apache-2.0
Add a package description, written to package.xml
Set the maintainer's email
Set the maintainer's name

commands.title: ros2 pkg xml
commands.desc: Print the package.xml contents of the specified package, for viewing package metadata such as dependencies, version, and license

commands.title: ros2 topic -h
commands.desc: Show help for topic commands
commands.notes: Shows all ros2 topic subcommands and usage; also works for subcommands, e.g. ros2 topic pub -h

commands.title: ros2 topic list
commands.desc: List all topics currently published/subscribed in the system

options.desc: Also show topic types
Show detailed info (including QoS settings and publisher/subscriber counts)

commands.notes: Filter with grep, e.g. ros2 topic list | grep chatter

commands.title: ros2 topic echo
commands.desc: Print messages published on a topic in real time; press Ctrl+C to stop

commands.title: ros2 topic info
commands.desc: Show detailed information about a topic, including its message type and publisher/subscriber counts; press Ctrl+C to stop

options.desc: Show detailed info (including QoS settings and publisher/subscriber counts)

commands.title: ros2 topic pub
commands.desc: Publish a message to a topic manually, once or continuously; message contents are passed in YAML format, and continuous publishing stops with Ctrl+C

options.desc: Publish once and exit
Publish continuously at 1 Hz (default 1 Hz)
Wait until N matching subscribers are found before publishing
Read message contents from a YAML file (e.g. the STDOUT of ros2 topic echo)

commands.notes:
Tip: after entering the topic name and message type, press Tab to auto-complete the YAML field template, edit the values, and press Enter to publish
Example:
  ros2 topic pub /turtle1/cmd_vel geometry_msgs/msg/Twist <TAB>

commands.title: ros2 topic hz
commands.desc: Display the topic publish rate, and check whether a topic publishes at the expected rate

commands.title: ros2 topic bw
commands.desc: Display the bandwidth used by a topic

options.desc: Maximum window size, in number of messages, for calculating the rate (default 100)
Seconds to wait for node discovery

commands.notes: Bandwidth reflects the receiving rate on the subscription side, which may be affected by platform resources and QoS settings, and may not exactly match the publisher's bandwidth

commands.title: ros2 topic find
commands.desc: List available topics of the specified message type

options.desc: Only display the number of matching topics

commands.notes: Filters topics by message type and outputs all matching topic names

commands.title: ros2 node -h
commands.desc: Show help for node commands
commands.notes: Shows all ros2 node subcommands and usage; also works for subcommands, e.g. ros2 node list -h

commands.title: ros2 node list
commands.desc: List all running nodes

commands.title: ros2 node info
commands.desc: Show detailed node information, including published/subscribed topics, services, and actions

commands.title: ros2 component container
commands.desc: Start a component container node
commands.notes: A container node runs multiple components in a single process, enabling node composition and zero-copy communication

commands.title: ros2 component list
commands.desc: List all components in a container node
commands.notes: Shows loaded components in the specified container node; without a container name, lists all

commands.title: ros2 component types
commands.desc: List available component types

commands.title: ros2 component load
commands.desc: Load a component into a container node

options.desc: Set the component node name
Remap topic/service names

commands.notes: Component types can be listed with ros2 component types; once loaded, the component runs inside the container node

commands.title: ros2 component unload
commands.desc: Unload a component from a container node
commands.notes: The component ID can be found with ros2 component list

commands.title: ros2 component standalone
commands.desc: Run a component as a standalone node
commands.notes: Runs in its own process, outside a container

commands.title: ros2 component nodes
commands.desc: List all running component container nodes

commands.title: ros2 component register
commands.desc: Register a component type with a container (without loading it)
commands.notes: Only registers the component type, so it can be loaded later by ID

commands.title: ros2 component unregister
commands.desc: Unregister a component type from a container; once unregistered, the type can no longer be loaded
commands.notes: The ID can be found with ros2 component list

commands.desc: Show detailed information about the specified service

commands.desc: Show the type of a service

commands.title: ros2 service find

commands.title: ros2 service call

options.desc: Print messages in flow style (no line breaks between fields)
Output all recursive fields separated by commas (for plotting)
Output arrays, bytes, and long strings fully without truncation
Truncate arrays, bytes, and strings to the given length (default 128)

commands.title: ros2 action list

options.desc: Also show action types

commands.desc: Show detailed information about the specified action, including its type and server/client node names

commands.desc: Show the type of an action

commands.desc: Send an action goal; goal values are passed in YAML format, and press Ctrl+C to stop waiting for a response

commands.title: ros2 param list
commands.desc: List all parameters of the specified node, including their names, types, and current values

commands.title: ros2 param set
commands.desc: Set a parameter value, supporting int, float, bool, string, list, and other types; press Ctrl+C to stop waiting for a response
commands.notes: After setting a parameter, the node receives a parameter update event that can be handled inside the node

commands.title: ros2 param get
commands.desc: Get a parameter value, showing its type and current value; press Ctrl+C to stop waiting for a response
commands.notes: Gets a parameter value from the specified node, useful for debugging and verifying parameter settings

commands.title: ros2 param dump
commands.desc: Save all parameters of the specified node and their values to a YAML file (you need to create the file manually or use the > operator), useful for backup and migration
commands.example: ros2 param dump /turtlesim > ~/Desktop/turtlesim.yaml  # Save current config to the desktop

options.desc: Specify the output directory

commands.title: ros2 param load

options.desc: Specify the node type

commands.title: ros2 bag -h

commands.title: ros2 bag burst

commands.title: ros2 bag convert
commands.desc: Convert a bag file into a new bag with the specified storage/serialization format

commands.notes: Converts storage/serialization formats, e.g. from rosbag1 (.bag) to sqlite3/mcap; use --output-options to set output options such as storage and serialization

Loop playback of the bag file
Start playback paused, requiring manual resume
Publish the /clock topic to synchronize time

options.desc: Specify the output directory / file prefix
Record service events for the specified services only
Record service events for all services

commands.title: ros2 bag reindex
